alternatives.text: • Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace

period. During this 7-day period, full platform access and compute services continue with zero service degradation.
• Day 3 & Day 6: Automated payment retry attempts are executed against primary and backup payment methods
  on file.
• Day 8 (Email Overdue Warning): Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, CloudScale transmits an
  automated formal Email Warning to the primary account owner and billing administrator stating the account is
  delinquent.
• Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to
  Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are
  blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
• Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5%
  (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.
• Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is
  formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.
• Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day
  recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data
  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
• Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer
  configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
 Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future

  Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are
  blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.

• Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day
  recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data
  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.

input_context: Treat the database as a fixed supplied snapshot. Its account/payment statuses are snapshot labels, not a historical status ledger. Do not infer a past account state from those labels. Use the stated policy versions for the exercise; do not invent later revisions.

For cases calculating monthly credits, assume all recorded downtime in the specified month is qualifying, non-overlapping downtime, that the incident list is complete for that month, and that subscriptions remained covered throughout that month. Assume other credit prerequisites and timely filing are satisfied unless the question explicitly asks about them or provides different facts. These are exercise assumptions, not facts recorded in the database.

For credit amounts, treat monthly_rate as the applicable final monthly recurring fee, already reflecting any contractual discount. Do not apply the 15% annual discount again. The database has no currency column: report amounts as currency units, unless the question supplies a currency. Ignore taxes for credit calculations.

Use actual calendar-month lengths in UTC: January and March 2024 have 44,640 minutes; February 2024 has 41,760 minutes. Do not use the SLA's illustrative 30-day allowance for every month. Compare unrounded uptime against bracket thresholds; round displayed uptime to six decimal places and money to two decimal places.

For annual refund-window questions, use subscriptions.start_date as initial activation for the exercise. Do not substitute customer join dates or renewal dates. The database does not prove new activation at renewal or record refund requests, compute usage, claim filings, or invoice due dates.

Cite both PDFs by document and page/section, and expose the SQL and its raw result. Use an actual calculator tool for arithmetic when exercising the full system. Equivalent read-only SQL and equivalent supporting passages are acceptable.

expected_database_response.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, c.tier, c.region,
       c.status AS account_status, s.subscription_id,
       s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate, s.start_date, s.renewal_date,
       s.payment_status, i.ticket_id, i.severity, i.downtime_minutes,
       i.reported_at, i.resolved_at, i.status AS incident_status,
       i.sla_breached
FROM customers AS c
JOIN subscriptions AS s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN incident_tickets AS i
  ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
 AND substr(i.reported_at, 1, 7) = :month
WHERE c.company_name = :company_name
ORDER BY s.subscription_id, i.ticket_id;

All enterprise subscriptions renew automatically at the expiration of the active billing period to guarantee uninterrupted
service:
• Monthly Plans: Renew automatically every 30 days unless cancelled at least 48 hours prior to the next billing
   date.

   customers receive updates every 2 hours.
• Severity 2 Incidents: Enterprise customers receive status updates every 2 hours; Professional customers
  receive updates every 6 hours.

3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
 Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future
 renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated
 refunds.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
95.00% to < 98.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      50% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
 CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:
 • Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial
    service activation date.
 • Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50
    computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes
    strictly non-refundable.
 • Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access
    continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
95.00% to < 98.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      50% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
 CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:
 • Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial
    service activation date.
 • Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50
    computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes
    strictly non-refundable.
 • Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access
    continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
 Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future
 renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated
 refunds.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
95.00% to < 98.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      50% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

WITH monthly_incidents AS (

• Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to
  Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are
  blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
• Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5%
  (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.
• Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is
  formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.
• Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day
  recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data
  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
• Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer
  configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

1.2 Out-of-Scope Systems & Applicability
This policy does not cover customer-developed application software, custom scripts running inside virtual
instances, external third-party software packages, client-managed external DNS configurations, or third-party
downstream APIs.
This policy applies to all active customer accounts in good standing governed by a signed CloudScale Master
Services Agreement (MSA) or an active online subscription plan.

6. Exclusions & Limitations
The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for
Service Credits:

8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid
   invoices or material violations of CloudScale’s Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

5.2 Sales Tax and Value-Added Tax (VAT) Regulations
All fees quoted and billed by CloudScale are exclusive of applicable taxes, statutory levies, and customs duties:
• United States Sales Tax: CloudScale collects applicable state and local sales taxes based on the customer’s

1.3 Automatic Subscription Renewal
All enterprise subscriptions renew automatically at the expiration of the active billing period to guarantee uninterrupted
service:
• Monthly Plans: Renew automatically every 30 days unless cancelled at least 48 hours prior to the next billing
   date.
• Annual Plans: Renew automatically for successive 12-month terms unless a written cancellation notice is received
   at least 30 calendar days prior to the annual contract expiration anniversary date.

3.1 Cancellation Submission Process
 Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/
 billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48
 hours prior to the next billing date.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice

< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.
